# `hostname`

`hostname` sets the node's host name, both the stored one
(`/etc/hostname`) and the running one, with `hostnamectl` on the node. It
does not edit `/etc/hosts`; if your servers need a line there, own that
file with a [`file`](file.md) node task.

## Inputs

- `name` (string; required): a short name or a fully qualified one, at most 64 characters; own /etc/hosts with a file task

## Outputs

The node task's result holds these fields. A later node task reads them as `.node_tasks.<id>.<field>`, where `<id>` is the node task's `id`.

- `status`
- `change`
- `value.hostname_before`
- `value.hostname_after`

## What a dryrun reports

Supported; reads the stored and the running host name and reports the name that would be set.

## Retries and time limits

Bounded automatic retries by default; retry: false turns them off.

The node task takes the time limits `time_limit` and `time_limit_per_try`; without them, the project's `node_task_defaults` apply. `mmx describe-module task` describes the settings every node task accepts.

## Examples

### Name the node after its inventory entry

```yaml
- hostname:
    name: "{{ .node.name }}.example.com"
```

On the node, this node task sets the host name `web01.example.com` for a
node named `web01` in the inventory. MMX inspects the node first and reports
unchanged when the node already has that name. A changed host name is
reported with the old and the new name.

## How it works

- `name` is a short name such as `web01` or a fully qualified one such as
  `web01.example.com`: letters, digits, and hyphens, in parts separated by
  dots, at most 64 characters.
- Results and dryrun show `hostname_before` and `hostname_after` in
  `.this_node_task.value`. `hostname_before` is the stored host name, or the
  running one on a node that has none stored.

## Errors and what they mean

| The reason holds | What the error means, and what to do |
|---|---|
| `hostnamectl is not installed; install the package systemd first` | Install the `systemd` package in an earlier node task. A dryrun reports the `hostname` node task not checked, because an earlier node task may install `hostnamectl`. |

## Tested on

**Distributions:** Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 10.

The suite `tests/integration/node_settings.py` runs on Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Rocky Linux 9, and AlmaLinux 10, in containers on the first four and in virtual machines on the last two. The
[validation record](../../changing-mmx/validation.md)
has the latest results.
